patch.value:
## The operation this is about

Asking for less output is the single most frequent thing an agent does with `pm`, and it is the operation with the least consistent surface in the product.

## Measured 2026-07-31 at HEAD, nineteen read commands

Eighteen distinct output-bounding flag spellings exist: `--after`, `--blocked-limit`, `--brief`, `--check-only`, `--compact`, `--counts`, `--depth`, `--fields`, `--for`, `--format`, `--full`, `--limit`, `--no-truncate`, `--section`, `--stream`, `--summary`, `--token-budget`, `--verbose`. No two commands expose the same set.

| command | bounding flags | spellings |
|---|---|---|
| list | 10 | after brief compact fields for format full limit no-truncate stream |
| context | 8 | after depth fields for format limit section token-budget |
| search | 7 | after compact fields for format full limit |
| get | 5 | depth fields for format full |
| next | 5 | blocked-limit for format limit token-budget |
| health | 5 | brief check-only full summary verbose |
| deps | 4 | format full summary token-budget |
| graph | 4 | after full limit summary |
| history | 4 | compact format full limit |
| activity | 4 | compact full limit stream |
| validate | 3 | counts full verbose |
| events | 2 | full limit |
| contracts | 2 | full summary |
| comments | 1 | limit |
| notes | 1 | limit |
| files, docs, stats, aggregate | 0 | — |

## Five asymmetries that matter more than the total

**Four read surfaces cannot be bounded at all.** `files`, `docs`, `stats` and `aggregate` expose zero bounding flags. Their output is whatever the workspace happens to be.

**`--limit` reaches 10 of 19.** The most basic bound in the product is absent from `get`, `deps`, `contracts`, `health`, `validate`, `files`, `docs`, `stats` and `aggregate`.

**`--fields` reaches 4 of 19** (list, get, search, context). Projection — the cheapest possible bound, because it costs the producer nothing — is unavailable on three quarters of read surfaces.

**`--token-budget` is on the wrong three.** It exists on `next`, `context` and `deps`. It does not exist on `list`, `get` or `search` — the three surfaces that declare and enforce per-intent token ceilings. So the one flag that could raise a ceiling is absent from exactly the surfaces whose ceilings have been measured as infeasible.

**`--summary` is on four and missing from the four that need it.** Present on `deps`, `graph`, `health`, `contracts`; absent from `list`, `get`, `next`, `context`. On `health`, four near-synonyms coexist — `--brief`, `--check-only`, `--summary`, `--full` — and an agent cannot infer from the names which produces the least output.

Widest pairwise disagreement: 10 flags (list) against 0 (files, docs, stats, aggregate).

## Composition has no declared algebra

`context` accepts five bounding dimensions simultaneously. `get --depth deep --for inspect` omits its result while either flag alone returns content. Nothing states which dimension wins when two disagree, so composition is discovered by experiment rather than read from a contract.

## The trend, which is the real argument

Every context capability shipped in the last month added a bounding flag and removed none. `--for` and `--token-budget` and `--section` are all recent. A consolidation programme that does not stop that trend has not simplified the surface, it has renamed it.

## The target

Reduce output bounding to **one declared dimension set, available identically on every read surface**:

1. **What to include** — field/section selection (`--fields`, subsuming `--brief`, `--full`, `--section`, `--compact`, `--counts`, `--check-only`, `--verbose`, `--summary`).
2. **How much of it** — row and traversal bounds (`--limit`, `--after`, `--depth`, subsuming `--blocked-limit`, `--sample-limit`, `--max-items`, `--no-truncate`).
3. **What it may cost** — `--token-budget`, with `--for` selecting a named preset over the other two.
4. **How it is encoded** — `--format`, with `--stream` as an encoding choice rather than a separate dimension.

Every existing spelling is retained permanently as a hidden alias onto that set — nothing is removed and no invocation breaks. Where a surface genuinely cannot support a dimension, the contract declares why, and the flag is accepted and reported as inapplicable rather than rejected as unknown.

A declared **precedence algebra** states which dimension wins when two disagree, so `--depth deep --for inspect` has a contract-defined result instead of an experimental one.

## Why this is the first tranche, before any noun is moved

Two independently recorded simplification axes on the parent epic reach the same conclusion from different directions: folding `list-*` into `list --status` is a null move while the flag lexicon is inconsistent, and folding nouns is a null move for an agent that must still learn a per-command availability matrix to ask for less output. This is the smallest self-contained tranche in the whole programme, it is the one an agent pays for on every single call, and unlike a noun count its metric cannot be improved by hiding spellings behind aliases.

## Metric

Not the total flag count. The **pairwise availability disagreement** between any two read surfaces over the declared dimension set — 10 today at its widest — and the count of read surfaces that support zero dimensions — 4 today. Target: 0 and 0. Both are computable from the contract table, so the gate is a contract test rather than a review.

## Relationship to adjacent owners

This is not the flag lexicon conformance item, which forbids two spellings for one concept anywhere in the CLI; this decides which bounding dimensions exist and requires them everywhere on reads. It is not the intent-scoped projection feature, which supplies `--for` presets over this set. It is not the output token budget contract, which declares the ceilings this set exposes. It is not the uniform output contract, which owns envelope shape and format grammar. All four consume or feed this set; none of them declares it.

One declared output-bounding dimension set on every read surface: 18 flag spellings across 19 commands collapse to include / how-much / cost / encoding, with a precedence algebra and permanent aliases
Consolidate every way to ask a pm read for less output into one dimension set available identically on all read surfaces, with declared composition precedence and zero removed spellings.

One declared bounding dimension set (include, how much, cost, encoding) is available identically on every read surface, or the contract states per surface why a dimension is inapplicable; Pairwise availability disagreement between any two read surfaces over the dimension set is zero, asserted by a contract test rather than reviewed; No read surface supports zero bounding dimensions; files, docs, stats and aggregate gain the set; A declared precedence algebra states which dimension wins when two are supplied, and get --depth deep --for inspect has a contract-defined result; Every one of the 18 current spellings continues to work as a hidden alias with a one-line migration hint; no invocation in any recorded transcript breaks; A gate fails when a new read command or a new bounding flag is added outside the declared set, so the growth trend stops rather than being periodically re-measured
Deliver a universal, fully-customizable PM tool whose baseline primitives (via the pm SDK) adapt to any project
Turns asking for less output from a per-command availability matrix into one learnable contract, which is the token cost every agent pays on every invocation.
An agent learns one bounding vocabulary once and applies it to every read surface in the product.

Two recorded simplification axes independently conclude that noun consolidation is a null move until output bounding is uniform; this is the smallest tranche and the one an agent pays for on every call.
